records.title: Write-off, waiver and compromise are separate stages
records.summary: RBI’s current commercial-bank directions define technical write-off as accounting derecognition without waiver of borrower claims. Compromise may involve an agreed sacrifice; settlements exceeding three months are treated as restructuring. Criminal proceedings and applicable penalties continue in fraud/wilful-default cases.
records.response: RBI frames settlement as discretionary commercial judgment to maximize recovery, not a borrower entitlement.
alternativeExplanations: Preserving a legal claim does not guarantee that recovery will occur.
records.falsifier: A specific settlement deed, court order or enacted waiver is required to classify a named borrower’s extinguished liability.

records.title: IBC recovery depends on the denominator and data stage
records.summary: At 30 June 2026 IBBI reports 1,484 resolution plans; Table 5 gives ₹435,469.89 crore creditor realization against ₹1,426,665.38 crore claims and ₹261,422.74 crore liquidation value. Published ratios are 30.52% of claims and 166.58% of liquidation value. The 94.72% fair-value comparison uses only 1,359 cases.
records.response: IBBI says realization excludes CIRP cost and various possible future recoveries, guarantees, equity and avoidance proceedings. Many debtors entered insolvency defunct.
alternativeExplanations: Claim value and liquidation value answer different questions; neither alone measures a policy counterfactual.
Some approved plans later enter liquidation or restart, and IBBI revises counts.
records.falsifier: Implementation and cash-distribution records are required to verify actual cash received by creditors.

geography.note: National fund, regulation or aggregate; no state spending allocation inferred.

limitations: Do not independently divide full-set realization by a fair-value subtotal based on a smaller set.
Do not add bank write-offs and IBC admitted claims; populations overlap.

records.title: Mahan: named resolution plan, new control and separate payment stages
records.summary: IBBI’s historical row 429 records Essar Power M P Limited: ₹12,723.60 crore total claims, ₹12,067.58 crore FC claims, ₹1,733.40 crore liquidation value and ₹2,500 crore realizable by FCs. Adani Power’s filed accounts separately report NCLT approval 1 November 2021, control acquired 16 March 2022, ₹600 crore upfront lender payment and ₹1 crore equity. These are distinct stages, not a single cash giveaway.
records.period: Plan approved 1 November 2021; acquisition 16 March 2022; IBBI snapshot September 2022; FY2022-23 issuer accounts
records.response: Issuer states conditions precedent were met and reports the acquired plant’s continued operation. Its consolidated business-combination note recognizes assets and liabilities; the transaction was not merely a ₹1 crore purchase of an unencumbered plant.
alternativeExplanations: A resolution transfers assets/control to a new investor; the old borrower’s claim shortfall is not automatically a benefit paid to its former promoter.
₹600 crore upfront is one payment stage; the plan-realizable ₹2,500 crore is a different measure.
records.falsifier: Original complete plan, distribution waterfall, deferred-payment schedule and subsequent lender receipts are needed to reconcile total realized recovery.

amounts.stage: amount realizable by financial creditors under plan; not NPV

geography.note: Mahan thermal plant at Bandhaura, Singrauli; project location, not parent-company headquarters or a statewide loan total.

limitations: No personal enrichment, political favor or unlawful waiver is inferred.
Neither table nor issuer excerpt proves current loan balances or all subsequent recoveries.
records.dateBasis: Acquisition/control event reported by issuer; approval was 1 November 2021 and financial table snapshot September 2022.
